claims.summary: For proper binary Boolean J_D, surviving degree-b weight w, free-coordinate candidate set S and V_K(S), let d_w(S,K)=dim[w V_K(S)]. A complete acyclic product-only source with t_a active constant rows per block admits a surviving wf and coherent constant map if sum_alpha,a R_a(alpha)2^(-t_a)<d_w(S,K), where R_a(alpha) uniformly bounds attainable nonzero input vectors over outside assignments conditional on every earlier row choice. All companions times f vanish on the full cube, and original degree-B replay fits b+K+B<=D. On a weighted free cube, q conditional outside Boolean features per ancestor cone suffice with t=ceil(log2(4M))+q and K=floor(|S|/2), giving an active fixed-depth polylog-degree regime on the growing family.
claims.assessment: Working elementary extension of support-density exclusion. The whole-source conditional union bound, bad-fiber dimension argument and original-degree replay passed one medium reviewer. No full outside-variable module or generic small-diversity claim. An independent outside affine tuple refutes automatic small fibers while admitting a different outside-dependent repair.
claims.rationale: Extends the existing supported-source mechanism to a globally supported conditional-feature class without coefficient interpolation. Supplies a scoped tool but no new unrestricted Frege exponent or family lower bound.
claims.next_action: Test a source-derived hybrid of outside affine removal and nonlinear fiber diversity, retaining the actual weighted denominator and original replay.

relationships: The old supported-input theorem is the special case R_a(alpha)<=1 with common active row count t. The new proof charges multiple attainable outside input vectors.
Its free-coordinate injectivity gives d_w(S,floor(s/2))>=2^(s-1); no action of outside variables on that carrier is assumed.
Related globally small-image construction interpolates maps and charges its recursion; current theorem instead uses conditional fibers, constant rows and a selected free-coordinate weight.
Uses the existing fixed graph family with D=Theta(n log²n) and log N=Theta(log²n) only to demonstrate an active fixed-depth window.
